name: collection_index
description: List every object of a delivered collection: size, modified time (UTC, to the nanosecond the file system holds; modified_epoch_ns is the raw value as a decimal string, because a JSON number past 2^53 does not survive a JavaScript or jq 1.6 reader), the SHA-256 of the whole file, and a hypothesis for the path the file had on the source machine. source_path_hypothesis is a convention's reading of the path in the collection (path, method, confidence low, medium or none, the components it could not explain, the other readings): a guess about a layout, never called the original path; a real root directory is kept, a Linux tree is rooted the same way with or without it, and a wrapper that needs the collector's own index (uploads/<accessor>/...) is not decoded. source_path_observed is filled only from a collector's own record: a KAPE copy log in the tree, matched by the row's DestinationFile ending with the file's path relative to that log's own directory (so a file outside it never claims the row), with the log, the row and the log's ModifiedOnUtc raw beside the delivered time; rows that name one source are one observation, rows that name different sources, or a sibling that shares the name letters of case apart, are ambiguous with every candidate listed, and none is nothing; a copy log with rows it cannot use makes the mapping partial; no other collector's records are read. A disk image, a memory capture or an archive in the root is indexed like any file and says what it looks like (object_class, from its first bytes and name; nothing is opened). Symbolic links are recorded and never followed, special files and empty directories are recorded, and every object that could not be listed, examined or read is a row with its error and makes the status partial. The complete census is written to a file in a job, with out_file, with a contains filter, and whenever the inline page cannot hold it (a page is bounded by bytes as well as by limit); a file already at the name is never replaced (this one is kept beside it as name.2.jsonl and named) and an out_file inside the collection is refused, by identity, so a case-variant spelling does not get round it. contains is read on what is printed, never on a withheld text, filters the inline page and the hashing only (the file holds every object with matches_filter, and files outside the filter say not_attempted), and a pattern that repeats a group that itself repeats is refused. More than 90% of more than 20 files on one UTC date is reported as mtime_distribution_anomaly with counts and no cause; the collector's recorded times, archive member times and the acquisition time are other clocks, not read here. possible_renamed_streams is a guess from file-name shape. Not measured: whether the tree is complete, whether a time is the source's or the copy's, a stream that was dropped. A name that marks a credential store (a password verifier file, a private key, a keychain, a saved-credential or browser store, DPAPI, hive logs; may_hold_secrets, a name hint only) is not hashed unless hash_credential_stores is true, which needs a job and write_values: true: its digest then goes only to the sealed values file, never to the answer or the index. Run it as a job with secret_output: true (the tool cannot see whether the job was run so). Paths are withheld where shaped like a recovery password, an access key, a token, a private-key block, URL user-info, or the value after a credential header, key name or password option; write_values: true (jobs only) writes the real strings to $OUT/collection-index-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created first, a second run in the same job refused. The answer starts with the summary and ends with the entries.

root.description: The collection directory (an archive is not opened: extract it into a job's output first)

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 2000 characters) over the path in the collection and over the hypothesis path. It filters the inline page and the hashing; the complete index file holds every object

hash.description: Hash every matching file (default true; false is much faster on a large tree, and each row then says it was not attempted)

hash_credential_stores.description: Hash the files whose names mark a credential store too (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; never copy such a digest into a post, a report or an indicator list

limit.description: Rows shown inline (default 200); the complete index is in the file complete_index names

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for the complete index, under work/ (in a job, under $OUT); refused inside the collection, outside the run directory or under inputs/, and never replacing a file that is there (the result is kept beside it and named)

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop the census after this long (default 3000, at most 3400): the answer then says it stopped, status partial, and how many directories were not listed

write_values.description: Write the real strings that were withheld to $OUT/collection-index-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the file is created first and one already there is refused
